items.title: Individualized mean arterial pressure during cardiac surgery The OPTIPAM Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether targeting an individualized mean arterial pressure (MAP) during cardiac surgery improves outcomes remains uncertain. The balance between improved perfusion and vasopressor-driven blood pressure augmentation is unclear. METHODS: In this single-blind, multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in 10 tertiary centers in France, adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned to either individualized MAP management (target within ±10% of preoperative baseline during surgery and for 24 h postoperatively) or standard management (target MAP ≥65 mm Hg). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute kidney injury, or prespecified neurologic complications within 7 days. Safety outcomes included hemorrhagic complications and transfusion requirements. RESULTS: A total of 172 patients were enrolled before the trial was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board because of increased bleeding in the individualized group. Mean intraoperative MAP was higher with individualized management (80.6 vs 75.6 mm Hg; P<0.001), despite limited target adherence (33% of intraoperative time) and greater vasopressor use. The primary outcome occurred in 27 of 85 patients (32%) in the individualized group and 25 of 87 (29%) in the standard group (relative risk, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.7 to 1.8; P=0.76). Hemorrhagic complications occurred more frequently in the individualized group (18% vs 3%; P=0.003). CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, it was not possible to determine whether an individualized MAP strategy reduced major postoperative complications. More bleeding complications were observed in the individualized group. Future studies should further investigate this safety signal when evaluating individualized blood pressure targets.

items.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
items.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate therapy on mortality and renal outcomes in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, 90-day mortality, RRT-free days, vasopressor-free days, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and adverse events. RESULTS: Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified. CONCLUSION: Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Further trials should define the patients most likely to benefit. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251246519.

items.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study.
items.abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care. METHODS: Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint. RESULTS: 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation. CONCLUSION: This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) Initiative, registration number 2320.

items.title: Short-term Modification of Postoperative Ventilation Phenotypes with Electrical Impedance Tomography-guided Positive End-expiratory Pressure Titration.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postoperative ventilation inhomogeneity is common after major surgery and has been associated with adverse outcomes. Whether these ventilation phenotypes can be acutely modified remains unknown. The authors investigated whether electrical impedance tomography (EIT)-guided positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration can improve ventilation homogeneity and cardiopulmonary function. METHODS: This prospective, single-center, nonrandomized feasibility study was conducted from August 2024 to June 2025. Sixty mechanically ventilated adults admitted to the intensive care unit after surgery at high risk of postoperative pulmonary complications underwent EIT assessment. Thirty with heterogeneous ventilation patterns (15 phenotype 1: ventral-dominant; 15 phenotype 3: dorsal-dominant) received individualized PEEP titration guided by dorsal fraction of ventilation (DFV) to achieve a homogeneous pattern (phenotype 2: DFV 50 to 59%), whereas 30 with homogeneous ventilation received no protocolized intervention. The primary endpoint was feasibility of achieving homogenization. RESULTS: Immediate phenotype conversion was achieved in 29 of 30 patients (96.7%; 95% CI, 82.8 to 99.9%). At 4 h, 28 of 30 patients (93.3%; 95% CI, 77.9 to 99.2%) remained within the target DFV range. In ventral-dominant patterns (n = 15), PEEP increased from 5 to 9 cm H 2 O; respiratory system compliance increased by 9.2 ml/cm H 2 O (95% CI, 6.1 to 12.3), and Pa o2 /fraction of inspired oxygen increased by 61.9 mmHg (95% CI, 8.6 to 115.2). In dorsal-dominant patterns (n = 15), PEEP decreased from 7 to 3 cm H 2 O; ventral compliance increased by 3.4 ml/cm H 2 O (95% CI, 1.1 to 5.8) without changes in global respiratory system compliance or oxygenation. Individualized PEEP reduced mean pulmonary artery pressure and increased cardiac index. Exploratory comparison showed severe postoperative pulmonary complications occurred in 25% of the interventional cohort and 41% of the historical cohort (absolute risk difference, -15.8% [95% CI, -38.8 to 2.2]; P = 0.17). CONCLUSIONS: Short-term modification of postoperative ventilation phenotypes is feasible with EIT-guided phenotype-directed PEEP titration. This strategy is associated with improved homogeneity and cardiopulmonary function, supporting regional ventilation as a therapeutic target.

items.title: Oxygen Delivery during Cardiopulmonary Bypass and Postoperative Mortality: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxygen delivery during cardiopulmonary bypass reflects the balance between pump flow, hemoglobin concentration, and arterial oxygenation and is a key determinant of tissue oxygen transport. While inadequate oxygen delivery has been linked to postoperative organ dysfunction, its association with mortality remains unclear. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including 4,358 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass at a tertiary center between 2018 and 2024. Time-weighted average indexed oxygen delivery (DO 2i ) was calculated from pump flow, arterial oxygen saturation, hemoglobin concentration, and body surface area. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI), stroke, and intensive care unit and hospital length of stay. Associations were evaluated using multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural factors. RESULTS: Lower intraoperative DO 2i was associated with higher 30-day mortality. Overall, 75 patients (1.7%) died within 30 days. Each 10-ml · min -1 · m -2 decrease in DO 2i was associated with increased odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio [OR adj ], 1.16; 95% CI, 1.09 to 1.23; P < 0.001). The adjusted 30-day mortality was 1.69% (95% CI, 1.32 to 2.05%) at the 25th percentile of DO 2i (226.2 ml · min -1 · m -2 ) compared with 0.74% (95% CI 0.41 to 1.07%) at the 75th percentile (295.6 ml · min -1 · m -2 ). Lower DO 2i was also associated with AKI (OR adj , 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.07; P < 0.001) and with longer intensive care unit (adjusted incidence rate ratio, 1.02; 95% CI, 1.01 to 1.03; P < 0.001) and hospital length of stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio, 1.01; 95% CI, 1.01-1.02; P < 0.001) but not with stroke (OR adj , 1.00; 95% CI, 0.95 to 1.06; P = 0.877). CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving lower intraoperative DO 2i during cardiopulmonary bypass had a higher risk of postoperative mortality, AKI, and prolonged recovery. These findings support the clinical relevance of oxygen delivery during bypass and provide a rationale for future mechanistic and interventional studies.

items.title: Association of Intraoperative End-tidal Carbon Dioxide, Ventilation, and Hypotension with Postoperative Mortality in Noncardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low intraoperative end-tidal carbon dioxide (ET co2 ) has been associated with increased postoperative mortality in retrospective studies. However, whether this association is independent of intraoperative hypotension, a strong predictor of mortality, and minute ventilation, a primary determinant of ET co2 , remains uncertain. The authors hypothesized that low intraoperative ET co2 is independently associated with postoperative mortality after adjustment for both intraoperative hypotension and minute ventilation. METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing noncardiac surgery during general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation between 2010 and 2020 at a tertiary care center. Primary exposures were intraoperative mean ET co2 , minute ventilation, and hypotension (severity and duration). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression estimated the independent association between ET co2 and mortality after adjustment for predefined confounders. An interaction between ET co2 and hypotension was tested. RESULTS: Among 185,455 patients (in-hospital mortality, 0.85%), lower intraoperative ET co2 was nonlinearly associated with increased mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 5-mmHg decrease from the median, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.86) independent of minute ventilation and hypotension. No significant interaction was observed between ET co2 and hypotension ( P = 0.19). Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In this large retrospective cohort, low intraoperative ET co2 was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality, irrespective of intraoperative hypotension and minute ventilation. These results suggest that ET co2 provides prognostic information beyond arterial pressure alone and may be a valuable marker for postoperative risk stratification.

items.title: Establishing curriculum priorities for intensive care recovery education: an international Delphi study.
items.abstract: PURPOSE: To effectively support recovery, intensive care unit (ICU) clinicians require training to identify patients at risk of post-intensive care syndrome and implement interventions during and after ICU admission. This study aimed to identify and prioritise curriculum topics for educating interprofessional ICU clinicians on evidence-based ICU recovery care across the continuum of critical illness. METHODS: A two-round e-Delphi study followed by a structured consensus meeting endorsed by the European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) was conducted. A steering committee generated an initial list of curriculum topics. In round 1, participants rated topic importance (9-point Likert scale) and suggested additional topics. In round 2, they rated newly identified topics and ranked priorities. Topics reaching consensus (≥70% rating as critical [7-9]; ≤15% rating as not important [1-3]) were discussed during the final consensus meeting. RESULTS: Participants' mean age was 43.5 (±10.5) years and they were predominantly female (n = 90, 66.7%). Priority topics included early mobilisation during ICU admission, post-intensive care syndrome, delirium prevention and management, implementation of the ABCDEF bundle, and cognitive support and rehabilitation. The final set of learning modules for a future curriculum was established. CONCLUSION: Priority topics and learning modules for an expert-developed curriculum framework for ICU recovery were established with interprofessional ICU clinicians through a structured international consensus process with moderate levels of participant retention between the two Delphi rounds and full consensus agreement among experts. This framework may support in delivering recovery-focused care across the continuum of critical illness.

items.title: Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients.
items.abstract: RATIONALE: High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF). In immunocompromised patients, ARF is the leading cause of ICU admission, yet a randomized trial found no overall benefit of HFNO in this population. OBJECTIVES: To assess whether baseline characteristics influence HFNO's effectiveness in preventing invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in immunocompromised patients with ARF. METHODS: A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Patients with a "do-not-intubate" order (n = 72) were excluded. Model performance was validated through 500 bootstrap iterations and patients were categorized into terciles based on predicted HFNO benefit. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients). MAIN RESULTS: Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores. In this subgroup, HFNO was associated with a significant lower incidence of IMV. In the observational cohort, the benefit-ranking performance was preserved, although absolute effect estimates were less calibrated. CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest HFNO might benefit specific immunocompromised patients with ARF. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

items.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID). RESULTS: SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles. CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

items.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI. MAIN TEXT: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent. CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes. HIGHLIGHTS: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. items.title: Optimizing Sepsis Time Zero Definitions Through Associations between Antibiotic Timing and Mortality.
items.abstract: RATIONALE: Sepsis performance measures require operational definitions of "time zero", but SEP-1's heterogeneous organ dysfunction criteria may not all identify patients vulnerable to harm from antibiotic delays. OBJECTIVES: To determine which SEP-1 organ dysfunctions identify patients in whom antibiotic delays are associated with increased mortality. METHODS: We analyzed adults with suspected infection using electronic health record data from 145 U.S. hospitals (2018-2023). We estimated associations between antibiotic timing (1-3 vs. 0-1h and 3-6 vs. 0-3h) and in-hospital mortality for each SEP-1 organ dysfunction criterion, alone and in combination: hypotension, elevated lactate, respiratory failure, renal dysfunction, hyperbilirubinemia, thrombocytopenia, and coagulopathy. We used inverse probability weighting to adjust for baseline and time-varying confounders. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 1,849,729 encounters with suspected infection, 624,416 had ≥1 organ dysfunction and received antibiotics within 6h of time zero. Antibiotics at 1-3 vs. 0-1h were associated with higher mortality when time zero was defined by hypotension (aRR 1.07; 95% CI, 1.03-1.10) or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L (aRR 1.10; 1.05-1.15), but not for other dysfunctions alone or in combination. Among patients without hypotension or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L, antibiotics at 3-6 vs. 0-3h were only associated with higher mortality in patients with acute respiratory failure (aRR 1.11; 1.05-1.18). CONCLUSIONS: Mortality associations with antibiotics beyond 1 hour were most evident when sepsis time zero was defined by hypotension or lactate ≥4.0mmol/L, and with antibiotics beyond 3 hours when defined by acute respiratory failure. These findings could inform refinements to sepsis time zero definitions to better guide antibiotic urgency and performance measurement.

items.title: Systemic Inflammation in Bronchiectasis: Data from the EMBARC-BRIDGE Study.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neutrophilic inflammation in the airways is associated with exacerbation risk in patients with bronchiectasis. Systemic inflammation and neutrophil function are less characterised. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between systemic inflammation and neutrophil function with severity of disease and clinical outcomes. METHODS: Observational international multi-centre study of adults with bronchiectasis (EMBARC-BRIDGE). Serum inflammatory profiling was performed in 487 patients using Olink® proteomics, and associations with key clinical and patient reported outcomes, including severe exacerbations during follow-up, were analysed. In a sub-study, peripheral blood neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients and controls were analysed for surface activation and functional markers, and functional responses including degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. RESULTS: Systemic inflammatory profiling revealed a dominant neutrophil-endothelial signature. Several proteins including PR3, AZU1, MPO, the soluble IL-33 receptor ST2, and the cellular stress marker GDF-15 were associated with increased disease severity using the bronchiectasis severity index, lower lung function, increased symptoms and for many markers, higher rates of severe exacerbations during follow-up. Neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients exhibited reduced surface CD11b and increased CXCR2, with lower CD11b correlating with lower lung function. Basal degranulation was reduced in bronchiectasis, whereas responsiveness to LPS stimulation was preserved. CONCLUSION: Bronchiectasis is associated with a systemic neutrophil and endothelial inflammatory signature linked to disease severity and risk of severe exacerbations, alongside altered but functionally-responsive circulating neutrophils.
